title: System Design
label: Systems
summary: Distributed systems, architecture patterns, reliability, security, and classic designs.

sections.title: System Design Interview Process & Requirements
sections.tagline: Start every design with clear requirements, scale, scope, diagrams, and interviewer alignment.
rows: When. The first 10 minutes of every system design round, before drawing boxes or naming technologies.
Key idea. A strong design answer is a structured conversation: clarify, estimate, design, validate, then discuss trade-offs.

subsections.title: Requirements & Scope
subsections.description: Functional requirements, non-functional requirements, scope control, and the HLD/LLD boundary.

subsections.title: Capacity Estimation
subsections.description: Back-of-the-envelope sizing for QPS, storage, bandwidth, peak traffic, and read/write ratio.

subsections.title: Architecture Diagrams & Communication
subsections.description: C4, UML, sequence/activity diagrams, and whiteboard layout strategy for clear interviews.

subsections.title: 5-Step Interview Framework
subsections.description: A repeatable flow for clarifying, estimating, designing, deep-diving, and closing with trade-offs.

subsections.title: Senior Engineer Signals
subsections.description: The communication habits that show ownership, trade-off thinking, and operational maturity.

subsections.title: Reference Numbers & Estimation Cheat Sheet
subsections.description: Numbers and shortcuts to make estimation fast without pretending false precision.

sections.title: Core System Design Fundamentals
sections.tagline: The vocabulary and trade-offs that every later topic builds on.
rows: When. Before choosing databases, queues, caches, or cloud services.
Key idea. Most design decisions are trade-offs among latency, throughput, consistency, availability, durability, and cost.

subsections.title: Latency, Throughput & Scalability Basics
subsections.description: Core performance terms, tail latency, vertical/horizontal scaling, and throughput trade-offs.

subsections.title: Availability, Reliability & SLAs
subsections.description: Reliability targets, downtime math, redundancy, and failover models.

subsections.title: Consistency Models
subsections.description: Strong, eventual, causal, monotonic, read-your-writes, and CRDT-based consistency.

subsections.title: CAP & PACELC Theorems
subsections.description: Partition trade-offs plus the latency-vs-consistency choice when the network is healthy.

sections.title: Networking, APIs & Traffic Management
sections.tagline: How requests enter, move through, and return from distributed systems.
rows: When. Any design with clients, APIs, load balancers, global routing, real-time updates, or public ingress.
Key idea. Good traffic design separates protocol choice, routing, load balancing, gateway policy, and overload protection.

subsections.title: HTTP, TLS & Protocol Fundamentals
subsections.description: HTTP versions, status codes, idempotency, TLS, and transport-level behavior.

subsections.title: API Styles: REST, GraphQL & gRPC
subsections.description: Choosing API contracts for public clients, internal services, streaming, and schema evolution.

subsections.title: DNS, Load Balancers & Traffic Routing
subsections.description: DNS resolution, records, GeoDNS, L4/L7 load balancing, health checks, and routing algorithms.

subsections.title: Proxies, API Gateways & Service Mesh
subsections.description: Forward/reverse proxies, API gateway responsibilities, L4/L7 differences, and sidecar/service-mesh patterns.

subsections.title: Rate Limiting Algorithms
subsections.description: Token bucket, leaky bucket, fixed/sliding windows, and distributed rate limiting.

subsections.title: Real-Time Communication: Polling, SSE, WebSockets & WebRTC
subsections.description: Choosing short polling, long polling, SSE, WebSockets, or WebRTC for real-time product requirements.

sections.title: Data Storage, Databases & Distribution
sections.tagline: How systems model, store, index, replicate, partition, and move data.
rows: When. Once entities, access patterns, consistency needs, and data volume are clear.
Key idea. Start from access patterns and consistency needs; then pick storage, indexes, replication, and partitioning.

subsections.title: Storage Types: Block, Object & File
subsections.description: Choosing block, object, file, blob, archive, and ephemeral storage for the workload.

subsections.title: SQL vs NoSQL Decision Framework
subsections.description: Choosing relational, document, key-value, wide-column, graph, time-series, or search stores.

subsections.title: ACID, Transactions & Isolation
subsections.description: Atomicity, consistency, isolation, durability, isolation levels, deadlocks, and two-phase commit.

subsections.title: Indexes & Query Optimization
subsections.description: B-trees, LSM trees, covering indexes, compound indexes, and query-plan thinking.

subsections.title: Replication & Read Scaling
subsections.description: Leader/follower, multi-leader, replication lag, read replicas, and failover implications.

subsections.title: Partitioning, Sharding & Data Distribution
subsections.description: Range/hash/directory partitioning, hot shards, rebalancing, and routing queries to shards.

subsections.title: Consistent Hashing & Rebalancing
subsections.description: Hash rings, virtual nodes, remapping behavior, and when consistent hashing beats modulo hashing.

subsections.title: NoSQL Internals
subsections.description: LSM trees, SSTables, quorum reads/writes, compaction, tombstones, and high-write data stores.

sections.title: Caching & Content Delivery
sections.tagline: Reducing latency and load with cache layers from process memory to the edge.
rows: When. Read-heavy systems, global content, expensive computations, hot keys, or slow origin services.
Key idea. Every cache needs a source of truth, invalidation policy, consistency story, and failure-mode plan.

subsections.title: Cache Strategies
subsections.description: Cache-aside, read-through, write-through, write-back, refresh-ahead, and where each belongs.

subsections.title: Cache Eviction, TTL & Invalidation
subsections.description: LRU/LFU/FIFO, TTL choices, explicit invalidation, and stale-while-revalidate patterns.

subsections.title: Cache Failure Modes & Pitfalls
subsections.description: Cache stampede, penetration, avalanche, hot keys, stale data, and memory pressure.

subsections.title: Redis & Distributed Caching
subsections.description: Redis structures, clustering, sharding, persistence, eviction, and distributed-cache design.

subsections.title: CDN Caching
subsections.description: CDN PoPs, origin shields, TTL, purges, signed URLs, and static content delivery.

subsections.title: Edge Delivery & Global Acceleration
subsections.description: Edge caching, invalidation, static vs dynamic acceleration, and token-protected edge access.

sections.title: Asynchronous Messaging & Event Streaming
sections.tagline: Decoupling systems with queues, logs, streams, delivery semantics, and event-driven flows.
rows: When. Work can happen later, spikes need buffering, or services should not call each other synchronously.
Key idea. Async design trades immediate consistency for resilience, throughput, and loose coupling.

subsections.title: Message Queues vs Event Streams
subsections.description: When to use task queues, pub/sub, append-only logs, and event streams.

subsections.title: Kafka Architecture
subsections.description: Topics, partitions, brokers, leaders, replicas, consumer groups, retention, and ordering.

subsections.title: Delivery Semantics & Reliability
subsections.description: At-most-once, at-least-once, effectively-once, idempotency, retries, and dead-letter queues.

subsections.title: Event-Driven Architecture
subsections.description: Event sourcing, CQRS, outbox pattern, choreography, and eventual consistency.

sections.title: Service Architecture Patterns
sections.tagline: How applications are decomposed into services, modules, and deployable boundaries.
rows: When. When the system grows beyond one codebase, one team, or one deployment lifecycle.
Key idea. Architecture boundaries should follow ownership, data, change rate, and failure isolation.

subsections.title: Monolith vs Microservices vs Serverless
subsections.description: Choosing deployment and ownership boundaries based on complexity, scale, and team structure.

subsections.title: Microservices Patterns
subsections.description: Service discovery, API composition, saga, outbox, sidecars, and database-per-service trade-offs.

subsections.title: Clean, Layered & Hexagonal Architecture
subsections.description: Keeping domain logic independent from frameworks, databases, transport, and infrastructure.

sections.title: Reliability, Resilience & Idempotency
sections.tagline: Designing systems that degrade gracefully instead of collapsing under failure.
rows: When. Any production design with dependencies, retries, overload, high availability, or partial failure.
Key idea. Assume every dependency fails; then bound blast radius, retry safely, and preserve core user value.

subsections.title: Circuit Breakers, Bulkheads & Timeouts
subsections.description: Preventing cascading failure with isolation, deadline propagation, and fast failure.

subsections.title: Backpressure, Throttling & Load Protection
subsections.description: Protecting systems from overload with rate limits, queues, adaptive throttling, and backpressure.

subsections.title: Graceful Degradation & Load Shedding
subsections.description: Dropping noncritical work, serving fallbacks, and preserving core flows under stress.

subsections.title: Distributed Locking, Idempotency & Safe Retries
subsections.description: Lease-based locks, fencing tokens, idempotency keys, deduplication, and retry correctness.

sections.title: Distributed Systems Coordination
sections.tagline: Coordination primitives for correctness across multiple machines.
rows: When. Leader election, consensus, distributed locks, distributed transactions, or cross-service consistency are required.
Key idea. Coordination improves correctness but costs latency, availability, and operational complexity.

subsections.title: Consensus Algorithms: Raft & Paxos
subsections.description: Replicated logs, majorities, leader terms, safety, liveness, and why consensus is expensive.

subsections.title: Leader Election, Heartbeats & Failure Detection
subsections.description: Detecting failed nodes, electing leaders, leases, split brain, and heartbeat trade-offs.

subsections.title: Distributed Transactions & Sagas
subsections.description: 2PC, sagas, compensation, outbox, and designing correctness across services.

sections.title: Search Systems & Discovery
sections.tagline: Indexing, ranking, autocomplete, and search-serving architecture.
rows: When. The product needs full-text search, discovery, typeahead, ranking, or geospatial lookup.
Key idea. Search is a separate read model optimized for retrieval, not a replacement for the source-of-truth database.

subsections.title: Search Indexing, Ranking & Typeahead
subsections.description: Inverted indexes, Elasticsearch/OpenSearch, BM25, and autocomplete architecture.

sections.title: Observability, SLOs, Testing & Delivery
sections.tagline: Knowing the system works and shipping changes without guessing.
rows: When. After the architecture is drawn, explain how you will operate, test, deploy, and debug it.
Key idea. A design is incomplete until it has telemetry, SLOs, safe rollout, and failure-verification plans.

subsections.title: Metrics, Dashboards & Alerting
subsections.description: Prometheus-style metrics, dashboards, alert routing, saturation, traffic, errors, and latency.

subsections.title: Logging & Distributed Tracing
subsections.description: Structured logs, correlation IDs, trace spans, sampling, and debugging across service boundaries.

subsections.title: SLOs, Error Budgets & Golden Signals
subsections.description: SLI/SLO/SLA definitions, error budgets, golden signals, and tracing-driven operation.

subsections.title: Testing, Chaos & Safe Deployment
subsections.description: Load, stress, soak, chaos testing, CI/CD, canary, and blue-green deployment.

sections.title: Security, Privacy & Threat Modeling
sections.tagline: Building systems that protect users, data, APIs, and infrastructure.
rows: When. Every design: mention auth, authorization, data boundaries, abuse cases, and sensitive operations.
Key idea. Security is a set of design constraints, not a final checklist after the architecture is done.

subsections.title: Authentication & Authorization
subsections.description: Sessions, JWT, OAuth/OIDC, RBAC/ABAC, least privilege, and service-to-service auth.

subsections.title: OWASP Top 10 & API Security
subsections.description: Injection, XSS, CSRF, SSRF, insecure design, API abuse, and secure-by-default endpoints.

subsections.title: Threat Modeling & Abuse Cases
subsections.description: STRIDE, attack surfaces, data classification, encryption boundaries, scraping, and credential-stuffing defenses.

sections.title: Cost & Performance Optimization
sections.tagline: Making trade-offs visible between speed, reliability, complexity, and money.
rows: When. After the baseline design works, or when constraints include budget, egress, latency, or operational load.
Key idea. Cost is an architecture property: compute, storage, network, managed services, and scaling choices all create it.

subsections.title: Cost Estimation & Build-vs-Buy Trade-offs
subsections.description: Compute, storage, egress, autoscaling economics, managed-service trade-offs, and cost/performance choices.

sections.title: Classic HLD Case Studies
sections.tagline: End-to-end designs that combine the primitives above into interview-ready systems.
rows: When. After the primitives are familiar; use these cases to practice complete designs and trade-off narration.
Key idea. Case studies are not templates to memorize; they are exercises in applying fundamentals under constraints.

subsections.title: Foundational Designs
subsections.description: URL shortener, Pastebin, rate limiter, typeahead, and other small systems that teach core primitives.

subsections.title: Core Interview Designs
subsections.description: Feeds, chat, video streaming, notifications, ticket booking, maps, payments, and message queues.

subsections.title: Advanced Senior-Level Designs
subsections.description: Uber, Google Search, collaborative editing, stock exchange, large feeds, and distributed locks.

sections.title: Low-Level Design & Object-Oriented Design
sections.tagline: Implementation-level design: classes, modules, interfaces, object models, UML, and design patterns.
rows: When. After the high-level architecture is clear, or whenever the interviewer asks for object models, APIs, schemas, or machine-coding design.
Key idea. HLD explains how services collaborate; LLD explains how code units collaborate. Keep the boundary clear.

subsections.title: HLD vs LLD Boundaries
subsections.description: Know which level of detail the interviewer is asking for.

subsections.title: Object-Oriented Foundations
subsections.description: The vocabulary for implementation-level design.

subsections.title: Design Principles
subsections.description: Rules that keep low-level designs simple and change-friendly.

subsections.title: UML & Interaction Modeling
subsections.description: Use diagrams to communicate object behavior, not decorate the answer.

subsections.title: Design Patterns For LLD
subsections.description: Use patterns as vocabulary for recurring object-design problems.

subsections.title: Machine Coding & LLD Case Studies
subsections.description: Practice turning requirements into maintainable code structure.

coverage.title: System Design Coverage Check
coverage.source: roadmap.sh System Design + System Design Primer + GeeksforGeeks System Design Tutorial
notes: Make trade-offs explicit: consistency, latency, cost, availability, and operability.
Use classic designs as integration practice, not memorized templates.
Add security, observability, and failure-mode reasoning to every design.
